newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses fall, hit by Wall St tumble.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses fall, hit by Wall St tumble.

text.p: European bourses fell sharply on Wednesday, weighed down by a wave of profit-taking on Wall Street which sent U.S. stocks tumbling to their biggest loss in five months.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened after its giddy rally to a 23-month peak against the mark on Tuesday. Sterling also fell on fears that its recent strength could harm British industry.
The losses on European bourses ended a record-breaking pace on much of the continent this week fuelled by investors who saw the recent strength of the dollar as a boon to exporters.

London, Frankfurt and Paris shares were unloaded as investors nervously digested Tuesday's close on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones industrial average lost 79.01 points, or 1.21 percent, to close at 6,442.69.
Big computer-driven sell programs in New York kicked in during a frantic last 10 minutes of trading to lock in profits after the Dow rose 500 points, or eight percent, in November.
"We haven't been following Wall Street up...we have been following it down...but I don't think it will be a disaster by any means," said a dealer in London.
But the gloom in London, where stocks fell 0.34 percent, was slightly offset by the the weaker pound which was seen as helping the exporting sector.
"Sterling is an important factor. If it weakens, it will help a lot of major stocks. So there are other things at work here besides Wall Street," the dealer said.
French stocks took the biggest knock from Wall Street, sliding 1.7 percent in early transactions after a strong performance this week.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down to 2306.79 points at one stage. Alcatel Alsthom fell 3.2 percent to 459.8 francs following news that the government has suspended the Thomson SA privatisation.
Frankfurt, which hit its fourth record close on Tuesday on the stronger dollar, fell 0.7 percent, sapped by Wall Street's fall and the weaker dollar.
"It's going to be consolidation today, based on where the dollar is going," one trader in Frankfurt said.
The dollar slipped under 1.56 marks in early trade, hitting exporting chemical and auto stocks. BMW, Hoechst and BASF were all lower after surging on Tuesday.
The U.S. currency slid by a pfennig in early European trading as the dollar took a breather after its record-breaking pace. It recovered a little by mid-morning.
"It had a very solid run and things are settling down. The currencies are pausing for breath after yesterday's massive move," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel.

Dollar was at 1.5605 marks in late morning, from 1.5647 on Tuesday, with the German currency drawing strength from figures showing Germany's economy expanded by one percent in the third quarter after a 1.5 percent increase in the previous quarter.

"They are pretty robust figures on the whole. After a very strong second-quarter the economy seems to be doing very well. It is definitely accelerating back to trend," said Klaus Baader, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

While the dollar weakened on profit-taking against the mark, yen, French franc and Swiss franc, attention switched to sterling as it struggled to recover after hitting a one-month low at 1.6410 against the dollar.
"We needed a good bout of profit-taking...Everyone went for the exit together," said the trader. The pound clawed back the early losses to stand at $1.6475 by late morning.

The pound's slide from four-year highs started on Tuesday when Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke said industry was starting to fret about the pound's exchange rate. Businessmen are worried that sterling's rally might damage British competitiveness by making exports more expensive.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.25 yen and 1.5605 marks against 113.68 yen and 1.5647 marks in late Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 22.1 points at 4,039.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 38.6 points at 2,310.51.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 20.91 points at 2,866..07.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $370.40 an ounce, compared to the close on Tuesday of $$367.85. Silver was firmer at $4.80, up nine cents.
